entrada.titulo: A secure and trustworthy blockchain-assisted edge computing architecture for industrial internet of things

perfil_anterior.problema: Low-power IoT devices may need help to handle the high processing demands of blockchain consensus methods
perfil_anterior.solucao: The proposed system, evaluated using MATLAB and Hyperledger Fabric, is not only efficient and reliable but also highly cost-effective.
perfil_anterior.avaliacao: The authentication time of proposed architecture with different nodes.
perfil_anterior.limites: The plan mostly depends on MEC servers’ dependability and accessibility, which might be problematic in areas with inadequate infrastructure or erratic connectivity
perfil_anterior.possibilidades: Avaliar o desempenho do PoAh em cenários de mobilidade de dispositivos IoT em cidades inteligentes.; Integrar mecanismos de identidade auto‑soberana (SSI) aos contratos inteligentes que utilizam PoAh.; Comparar o PoAh com outros consensos leves (e.g., Proof of Authority, Proof of Stake) em termos de consumo energético.; Aplicar criptografia baseada em atributos (ABE) para controle de acesso granular nos dados armazenados na blockchain.; Testar a arquitetura em ambientes de borda heterogêneos com milhares de nós para validar escalabilidade.

entrada.texto:

PoAh effectively tackles the two main flaws in the existing blockchain consensus: the network’s 51% attack 
and erratic network connection. While only trustworthy nodes can authenticate blocks in PoAh, any network 
device may produce blocks. This selective notification of peers about adverse circumstances resulting from these 
shortcomings ensures a more secure system. Blocks can only be added to the chain and authenticated by trusted 
peers, and the dynamic nature of trust values effectively addresses PoW’s vulnerability to a 51% assault. One of 
the main advantages of the proposed blockchain model is the traceability of unauthorized access. The proposed 
consensus model based blockchain network transaction Ttxr can be able to get the random message shared 
( PID i,j ) by any node in the network (Ni,j ). If any IoT node is originated to share any illegal message, then the 
proposed IoT will send back illegal message back to Ttxr . This will ensure by the public key of the node (Ni,j ), 
then the real node identity is calculated as follow as:
 RID i,j = hash(msg.publickey ) ⊕ PID i,j
For the above analysis we can prove that our proposed model can easily trace the origin of any illegal activity.
Performance evaluation of industrial operations
The efficiency study of the proposed blockchain structure, as demonstrated in this section, is crucial for 
understanding the potential impact of blockchain on industrial procedures. The service time required for 
various industrial procedures, which was assessed through several trials, is a key metric in determining the 
efficiency and practicality of the proposed blockchain structure. The duration of a task, comprising run-time 
or system processes executed on the computer’s behalf, is the task’s running time or processor time. The five 
industrial processes carried out by the system at hand are gathering data, movement, information from sensors 
capturing, device authentication, user authentication, and device identification. In this study, we used a Core i5 
desktop computer to conduct thorough simulations in Python to separate consumers, components, documents, 
and controllers into distinct groups and record the service’s execution time. We go over each operation’s service 
duration in the sections that follow.
First, we examine the enrollment procedure for blockchain-enabled intelligent industrial networks, a crucial 
step in establishing a secure and efficient network. There are five groups of users, with 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 
members each. A single user’s registration procedure consists of three primary steps: submitting a transaction 
request, authenticating the purchase, and updating the blockchain after successful verification. The first group’s 
execution time records a minimum of 815 milliseconds and a high of 1571 milliseconds. For the first group, 
the median time of execution is 963 ms. The bar graph in Fig. 5 compares the service time required for the 
various user groups, providing insights into the scalability and performance of the enrollment procedure. The 
comparison shows that more execution time was needed as the number of users increased. With fifty users, 
the fifth group is thought to be the largest. This group’s average time is 963 milliseconds. The user enrollment 
procedure responds quickly overall, which is a positive indicator of the efficiency of the proposed blockchain 
structure.
The sensor’s data-capturing procedure is examined in the third stage. Immutable information storage is one of 
the most essential features of blockchain-enabled technologies. The sensors for the suggested solution are divided 
into five groups, each with 10, 25, 50, 75, and 100 devices. Sensor identification, data encryption, transactional 
operation, and sensor data retention based on the device ID are the four steps of the blockchain network’s storage

resposta.resumo: O trecho descreve o consenso PoAh combinado com ECDSA, que melhora a segurança contra ataques de 51% e conexões instáveis em redes IIoT, detalha a rastreabilidade de mensagens ilegais e apresenta avaliação de desempenho de processos industriais, como tempo de inscrição de usuários (815‑1571 ms) e captura de dados de sensores (≈1908 ms).

evidencias.afirmacao: User enrollment time remains under 1 s even with 50 users.
evidencias.citacao: The first group’s execution time records a minimum of 815 milliseconds and a high of 1571 milliseconds

resposta.interpretacao: O consenso PoAh, ao combinar ECDSA e valores de confiança dinâmicos, parece oferecer resistência a ataques de maioria e melhorar a confiabilidade em redes IIoT com conectividade irregular, ao mesmo tempo em que mantém tempos de operação aceitáveis para processos industriais críticos.
